chapter_title: Yoga — A Way of Life (Sports and Wellness)
subject: English
period_schedule_display:
Period schedule:
  Row 1: 40 minutes × 4 periods = 160 minutes
Total: 4 periods · 2h 40min

periods.activity_title: Reading the Yoga Text and First Discussions

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Let us read (p.121): paired warm-up — what students know about yoga.
Let us discuss (p.124): fill blanks with words from the box.

time_bands.activity: Open with paired sharing on what students already know about yoga and International Yoga Day. Take two or three brief whole-class responses to activate prior knowledge before reading begins.
Read the informational text aloud together, pages 121–124, with students following along. Pause briefly at the Sanskrit shloka and the WHO mYoga reference to ensure comprehension of key terms.

Students work on the “Let us discuss” fill-in-the-blank activity (p.124) using the word box [sleep / lifestyle / health / strength / calm / stress / balance]. Review answers as a class, asking students to read each completed sentence aloud and justify their word choice.

periods.teacher_notes: This text traces yoga from its Sanskrit root ‘yuj’ through Patanjali’s Yoga Sutras to its global recognition via the WHO mYoga app — ensure students understand these connections when they encounter the passage. A common difficulty is conflating the physical and mental benefits; prompting students to sort benefits into two columns during discussion can sharpen this. Students who finish the fill-in task early may re-read the shloka passage and list two words they find unfamiliar.
materials: Textbook, Yoga — A Way of Life, pp. 121–127

periods.activity_title: Deeper Comprehension and Listening for Truth

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Let us think and reflect (p.124): discuss the aim of yoga and idea of unity.
Let us listen (p.125): select four true statements from the table.

time_bands.activity: Lead a whole-class discussion on two questions from “Let us think and reflect” (p.124): first, the aim of yoga as quieting the mind, then the idea of unity — between mind and body, thought and action, and human beings and nature. Encourage students to support their answers with specific words or phrases from the passage.

Read the listening transcript aloud at a measured pace (p.129 transcript: a girl describing her yoga practice with her grandfather). Students listen and mentally note which statements from the table are true.
Students write their four selected true statements, then share with a partner. Review as a class, reading each statement and asking for a show of hands before confirming the answer.

periods.teacher_notes: Having read about yoga’s unity of mind and body, students should be well-positioned to discuss what it means for the mind to ‘quieten’ — a phrase from the Yoga Sutras section. A common confusion in the listening task is between the grandfather’s age (65) and when he began practising yoga (age 16); draw attention to this distinction when reviewing answers. Students who are uncertain may re-read the transcript passage silently before discussion closes.
materials: Listening transcript (p.129 of the chapter PDF)

periods.activity_title: Sharing Yoga Thoughts and Writing a Benefits Paragraph

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Let us speak (p.126): groups of four share personal yoga thoughts in turns.
Let us write (p.127): guided paragraph on the benefits of yoga using sentence starters.

time_bands.activity: Form groups of four. Each student takes an uninterrupted turn to share their “yoga thoughts” (p.126) — whether they have tried yoga or not — using the provided sentence frames as scaffolds. Listeners are asked to note one idea they found interesting in a neighbour’s turn.
Brief whole-class share-back: one or two groups offer the most interesting idea they heard. This links spoken content to the written task that follows.

Students write a short paragraph on “The Benefits of Yoga” (p.127), using the provided sentence starters for opening, supporting, and concluding sentences. Teacher circulates, prompting students to include at least one physical and one mental benefit drawn from the text.
Two or three volunteers read their paragraph aloud. The class offers one positive comment each. Paragraphs are kept for personal reference.

periods.teacher_notes: The informational text distinguishes physical, mental, and systemic benefits of yoga — students should be encouraged to draw from all three categories when writing, not just list asanas. A common weakness in guided paragraph writing is a missing concluding sentence; remind students that the sentence starters include a closing frame. The speaking activity works best when the teacher gently ensures quieter students take their turn rather than deferring to more confident peers.

periods.activity_title: Practise vs Practice, Word Play, and Asana Exploration

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Let us learn (p.125): fill blanks with correct form — practice (noun) or practise (verb).
Let us explore (p.127): find two asanas and their benefits, share findings.

homework.task_brief: Let us learn (p.125): write two sentences each using advice (noun) and advise (verb).

time_bands.activity: Introduce the noun-verb pair ‘practice’/‘practise’ using the extract on page 125. Students complete the six fill-in-the-blank sentences, then read their answers aloud. Discuss how to test the correct form: substituting a clearly noun-only or verb-only word to check if the sentence still works.

Students work in pairs to find out about two yoga asanas — using textbook references on pages 121–127 and any knowledge they already have. Each pair prepares a brief spoken description: the asana name, how it is performed in broad terms, and one documented benefit.

Three or four pairs share their asana findings with the class. The teacher notes the asana names on the board and draws out any connection to the physical, mental, or systemic benefits described in the text. Homework for ‘advice’/‘advise’ sentences is explained.

periods.teacher_notes: The noun-verb distinction between ‘practice’ and ‘practise’ parallels ‘advice’/‘advise’ — a pattern worth naming explicitly so students can generalise. A common error is using ‘practise’ (verb) where a noun is required; the substitution test (try ‘habit’ or ‘routine’ — only a noun fits) is a reliable classroom strategy. Students who want to explore further may look up the Hatha Yoga Pradipika shloka referenced in the passage for additional context on asana practice.

items.source_lo: Student locates specific information and explains key concepts using an informational text as the vehicle.
items.source_context: Yoga's origins, the Sanskrit root 'yuj', Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, physical and mental benefits, WHO mYoga app.
items.item_stem: According to the text on yoga, the word 'yoga' comes from the Sanskrit root 'yuj'. Which of the following best describes what this root word means?

options.label: A
options.text: To stretch and strengthen the body through repeated movement.

options.label: B
options.text: To join or unite, symbolising harmony between mind and body.

options.label: C
options.text: To breathe deeply and calm the nervous system.

options.label: D
options.text: To follow the rules set by Sage Patanjali.

what_each_option_reveals.A: Student associates yoga with its physical dimension rather than its etymological meaning.
what_each_option_reveals.C: Student confuses the breathing technique aspect of yoga practice with the meaning of the word itself.
what_each_option_reveals.D: Student conflates Patanjali's contribution to systematising yoga with the origin of the word.

items.source_lo: Student locates specific information and explains key concepts using an informational text as the vehicle.
items.source_context: Yoga's origins, the Sanskrit root 'yuj', Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, physical and mental benefits, WHO mYoga app.
items.item_stem: The text states that the WHO launched the mYoga app in June 2021 as a free tool to promote yoga worldwide. What does this global initiative tell you about the importance the world now places on yoga? Use evidence from the informational text to support your answer.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer: The WHO's launch of the mYoga app shows that yoga is now recognised globally as a valuable tool for physical and mental health, not just a traditional Indian practice. By making it free and accessible worldwide, the WHO endorses yoga's documented benefits — such as stress reduction, improved flexibility, and better heart health — as important for global public wellness.

items.source_lo: Student identifies accurate information from a spoken account and distinguishes true statements from false or distorted ones.
items.source_context: A girl's spoken account of practising yoga with her grandfather, his age, park observations, and summer plans.
items.item_stem: Read the statements below about the girl's spoken account of her yoga practice with her grandfather. Write True or False for each statement.

options.text: The girl does simple yoga exercises together with her grandfather.
The girl's grandfather began practising yoga when he was sixty-five years old.
The girl uses breathing exercises to feel calm before a competition.
The girl plans to learn asanas from her grandfather during the winter vacations.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer:
1. True — the girl says she does simple yoga exercises with her grandfather.
2. False — the grandfather began practising yoga at the age of 16, not 65; 65 is his current age.
3. True — she says she does breathing exercises on the morning of an Inter-House competition to relax and feel focused.
4. False — she plans to learn asanas during the summer vacations, not the winter vacations.

items.item_stem: In the spoken account, the girl says that going to the park with her grandfather has an effect on her own yoga practice. In one or two sentences, explain what she observes at the park and how it influences her.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer: At the park, the girl sees many people — young and old — doing yogic breathing exercises. Watching them reinforces her own interest in doing these exercises, and she now uses them herself on the mornings of Inter-House competitions to feel relaxed and focused.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer:

items.source_lo: Student applies the noun-verb spelling distinction of words sharing a root using an informational text as the vehicle.
items.source_context: Noun-verb pairs practice/practise and advice/advise as they appear in the yoga text context.
items.item_stem:
The words 'practice' (noun) and 'practise' (verb) look similar but function differently in a sentence, just like 'advice' and 'advise'. Read the two sentences below and explain in your own words how you can tell which form — noun or verb — belongs in each blank. Then write one original sentence of your own using 'practise' correctly in the context of a wellness activity.

Sentence A: A regular _____________ of yoga can improve your posture over time.
Sentence B: Athletes are advised to _____________ controlled breathing before a race.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer: In Sentence A, 'practice' (noun) is correct because it follows the article 'A' and functions as the subject of the sentence — a noun slot. In Sentence B, 'practise' (verb) is correct because it follows 'to' (the infinitive marker), making it a verb. A student's original sentence should use 'practise' as a verb in a wellness context, for example: 'I practise yoga stretches every morning to stay flexible.'

items.item_stem: The text mentions that the United Nations General Assembly declared 21st June as International Yoga Day in 2014. Choose one yoga asana that you have read or heard about. Write a short description explaining: (a) the name of the asana, (b) the main steps involved, and (c) one specific benefit it is known for.

expected_elements: Names a specific asana correctly — e.g., Tadasana, Vrikshasana.
Describes two or more steps involved in performing the asana.
States one clear, specific benefit supported by known information.

items.source_lo: Student researches and presents findings on a topic extending the informational text into real-world practice.
items.source_context: International Yoga Day history, Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilisation seals, UNGA 2014 resolution, two asanas and their benefits.
items.item_stem: The informational text notes that seals from the Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilisation (around 2700 BC) suggest yoga existed in ancient India, and that 193 nations of the United Nations voted to establish International Yoga Day. Design a one-page project plan — in the form of a brief outline — for a classroom display on the history and global journey of yoga. Your outline should include: the title of the display, three sections you would include, and one image or artefact you would feature in each section.

expected_elements: Proposes a clear, relevant display title connected to yoga's history.
Identifies three distinct sections covering ancient, modern, and global dimensions.
Suggests a specific, appropriate image or artefact for each section.
Outline is logically sequenced and written in clear, brief notes.
